about: Final adversarial C7 lock / audit (2026-11-16). Generated by research/tools/c7_lock_source.py.

source.read: the published PRL, Phys. Rev. Lett. 122, 158302 (2019): the typeset PDF deposited at NSF PAR record 10101033 (labelled "Accepted Manuscript" on the PAR page; it carries the PRL header, pages 158302-1 to -6, the APS copyright line and the production line 0031-9007=19=122(15)=158302(6)). The APS site itself was not accessed: the PDF needs a subscription and the public link returned a bot challenge; neither was circumvented.
source.eq2: Accounting for the polynomial approximation error ‖yθ − pN−1‖∞, where ‖·‖∞ is the L∞ norm on [−1, 1], we can define a hyperellipsoid HY that must enclose model manifold Y, where the cross-sectional widths are given by ℓj(HY) = 2rσj(X) + 2‖y − pN−1‖∞. (2)
source.eq2Change: the only difference from arXiv v1 is the subscript of the error term (pN−1 instead of pN); the geometric claim is the same
source.radius: By Eq. (5), we have that ‖c̃‖2 < 4M√(4N − 3). This implies that the polynomial manifold P is bound in a hyperellipsoid HP. By Eq. (1), we have that ℓj(HP) = 8M√(4N − 3)σj(X).
source.corrections: Crossref (DOI 10.1103/PhysRevLett.122.158302): no updated-by entry and an empty relation list; a web search found no erratum, correction or corrigendum; arXiv has only v1; the APS article page could not be opened here.
source.correctionVerdict: No official correction was located in this audit.

eq2.verdict: Counterexample to Eq. (2) as written under the ordinary Euclidean prediction-space interpretation.
why: the sampled error lies in the box [−ε, ε]^N; for a Euclidean unit u, sup_(e in the box) uᵀe = ε‖u‖₁ with 1 ≤ ‖u‖₁ ≤ √N (C7Lb)

example (ii), distinct singular values, t = (−1, 0, 1): y_θ = θ_a(T₀ + T₂)/√2 + θ_eT₄; σ(X) = (2, √2, √2), first axis (1, 0, 1)/√2; the Eq. (2) ellipsoid value at θ = (99/100, 1/10) is 1.0249 > 1 (C7Lc)

even if the error were a Euclidean ball (a reading the paper's sup-norm bound does not give), containment in the ellipsoid with semi-axes rσ_j + δ fails for unequal axes: value 1.1493 > 1 for a = (1, 1/10), δ = 1/10 (C7Ld)
eq2.notClaimed: not "the published paper is wrong" in every reading: under a reading where "cross-sectional width" means a directional width along the axes AND the error is a Euclidean ball of radius ε, the widths 2rσ_j + 2ε are correct; that reading does not match the paper's sup-norm error bound
eq2.wording: exact wording of the verdict: "Counterexample to Eq. (2) as written under the ordinary Euclidean prediction-space interpretation."

constant.verdict: internal constant inconsistency / likely typographical factor; not a new mathematical result
facts: |c̃_0| ≤ M and |c̃_j| ≤ 2M give ‖c̃‖₂² ≤ M² + 4M²(N − 1) = M²(4N − 3), so ‖c̃‖₂ ≤ M√(4N − 3) (C7Lf)
the printed ‖c̃‖₂ < 4M√(4N − 3) is valid but loose by exactly 4, and the printed ℓj(HP) = 8M√(4N − 3)σj(X) is consistent with that loose radius (C7Lf)
Eq. (8)'s first term equals 2·M√(4N − 3)·√Nρ^(−j+2)/√(ρ² − 1): it uses the TIGHT radius; the printed radius would give 4× Eq. (8) (C7Lg)
Eq. (8)'s second term 4Mρ^(−N+1)/(ρ − 1) = 2ε is the additive Eq. (2) error term and inherits its issue (C7Lg)

geometry.exact: Y(Θ) ⊆ H_P ⊕ [−ε, ε]^N (Quinn's ball form) and Y(Θ) ⊆ V_mD_m·[−1, 1]^m ⊕ [−R_m, R_m]^N (box / zonotope form): Minkowski sums, not ellipsoids in general
width_u(Y) ≤ width_u(H_P) + 2ε‖u‖₁ = 2r‖Xᵀu‖ + 2ε‖u‖₁; along the j-th axis of H_P: 2rσ_j + 2ε‖u_j‖₁ ≤ 2rσ_j + 2√N ε; zonotope form 2‖D_mV_mᵀu‖₁ + 2R_m‖u‖₁
H_P ⊕ [−ε, ε]^N ⊆ E(2(AAᵀ + Nε²I)), A = rX: semi-axes √2·√(r²σ_j² + Nε²); proof by support functions, h_(E(Q))(u) = √(uᵀQu) ≥ ‖Aᵀu‖ + δ; the √2 cannot be dropped in general
the ellipsoid with semi-axes rσ_j + ε: does NOT contain Y in general (C7Lc), and does not contain H_P ⊕ B₂(ε) for unequal axes (C7Ld)

analyticity.statement: With z = e^(iφ), φ = α + iβ, |z| = e^(−β): the annulus ρ^(−1) < |z| < ρ is the strip |Im φ| < log ρ, and x = (z + z^(−1))/2 = cos φ maps it 2-to-1 (z ↔ 1/z) onto the open region bounded by E_ρ, the unit circle folding onto [−1, 1]. Exact equivalence: f is analytic in the open region bounded by E_ρ with |f| ≤ M ⟺ F = f∘cos is analytic in |Im φ| < log ρ with |F| ≤ M; such an F is automatically 2π-periodic and even. Conversely an analytic, 2π-periodic, EVEN F on the strip descends to such an f (Laurent coefficients g_(−k) = g_k, G = g_0 + 2Σ g_kT_k(x)). Without evenness the descent fails (sin φ).
analyticity.supersedes: pass 1: "strip analyticity of F_θ is Bernstein-ellipse analyticity of f_θ" (C7-B) — correct only with the even, 2π-periodic hypothesis stated, which F = f∘cos satisfies automatically

conventions.statement: exact axes σ(VD) = {√N r_0} ∪ {√(N/2) r_k} hold for Gauss–Chebyshev (first-kind) nodes x_i = cos((i + 1/2)π/N), i = 0…N − 1, with the unweighted Euclidean metric; they fail for Chebyshev–Lobatto (extrema) nodes unless the weights (1/2, 1, …, 1, 1/2) are used (norms N − 1 at k = 0, N − 1, (N − 1)/2 otherwise)

"exactly √N × the envelope" holds in the complex basis e^(ikt), |k| ≤ K, with an envelope on the complex coefficients and 2K + 1 ≤ N equally spaced samples (each r_k twice for ±k); in the real basis (1, cos kt, sin kt) the axes are √N r_0 and √(N/2) r_k; the Nyquist mode (N even, k = N/2) is degenerate and excluded; modes alias mod N

d_m(F; C[−1, 1]) = inf_(dim L = m) sup_(f∈F) inf_(g∈L) ‖f − g‖∞ ≤ R_m = Σ_(k≥m) r_k with L_m = span{T_0, …, T_(m−1)}; for this L_m the bound is attained (1/(θ − x) at θ = 2, x = 1), so the index cannot shift to R_(m+1); a function-space width, not a prediction-space ellipsoid axis

theorem.name: C7-R (final, locked)
hypotheses: a family F = {f_θ} ⊆ C[−1, 1] with a family-wide envelope |a_k(θ)| ≤ r_k on its Chebyshev coefficients (= the cosine-Fourier coefficients of F_θ(φ) = f_θ(cos φ)), Σ r_k < ∞
sample points x_1…x_N ∈ [−1, 1]; prediction space ℝᴺ with the Euclidean metric
conclusions: (1) sup_θ ‖f_θ − Σ_(k<m) a_k(θ)T_k‖∞ ≤ R_m = Σ_(k≥m) r_k, so d_m(F; C[−1, 1]) ≤ R_m (N-free)
(2) exact enclosure: Y(Θ) ⊆ V_mD_m·[−1, 1]^m ⊕ [−R_m, R_m]^N (a Minkowski sum)
(3) directional widths: width_u(Y(Θ)) ≤ 2‖D_mV_mᵀu‖₁ + 2R_m‖u‖₁ for every Euclidean unit u
(4) conservative ellipsoid: Y(Θ) ⊆ E(2(m·V_mD_m²V_mᵀ + N R_m² I)), semi-axes √2·√(mσ_j(V_mD_m)² + NR_m²)
(5) at Gauss–Chebyshev (first-kind) nodes, unweighted: σ(V_mD_m) = {√N r_0} ∪ {√(N/2) r_k : 1 ≤ k < m}, m ≤ N
(6) with a geometric envelope from uniform analyticity in E_ρ (equivalently, uniform analyticity of the even, 2π-periodic F_θ in |Im φ| < log ρ): R_m = 2Mρ^(1−m)/(ρ − 1)
(7) every object in (1)–(6) is defined from the function set, the sample points and the metric, hence unchanged by reparametrizations that keep the set

proof: one parameter, θ = aφ: g_φ = a²g_θ, while the function set, its coefficients, the envelope and the prediction image are unchanged (C7Lm)

several parameters, θ = θ₀ + A(φ − φ₀) with the domain mapped accordingly: g_φ = Aᵀg_θA, and A = g_θ^(−1/2)Λ^(1/2) realizes ANY positive spectrum Λ at that point; for F-C at θ = (1, 2): spectra (1, 1), (1, 1e12) and (5, 7) (C7Lm)
every output-side object is a function of the set and stays fixed (C7Lo), so it cannot determine a quantity that varies arbitrarily within the same set

lowerBound.statement: Envelope alone ⇏ nonzero actual-width lower bound.
lowerBound.proof: the envelope is an upper constraint; for every envelope with r_0 > 0 and every η > 0 the family θ·(η/2√N)·T_0, θ ∈ [0, 1], satisfies it with image diameter < η and all further widths 0; the singleton {0} satisfies it with all widths 0 (C7Ll)
